nodes.label: NetworkIsolationGatekeeper (Edge AI Egress Sandbox)
nodes.rationale: Whitelists only localhost, 127.0.0.1, firestore.googleapis.com, identitytoolkit.googleapis.com and *.firebaseio.com/firebaseio.com so legitimate Firebase sync still works while all other outbound egress (fetch, XHR, sendBeacon, WebSocket, EventSource) is blocked during local Edge AI PHI inference; parses canonical WHATWG URL hostnames and fails closed (returns true/blocked) on any malformed or unparsable input to prevent PHI exfiltration through substring or object-type spoofing.

nodes.label: Sandbox Escape Vulnerability: URL Object & Substring Spoofing Bypass
nodes.norm_label: sandbox escape vulnerability: url object & substring spoofing bypass
nodes.rationale: window.fetch's interceptor only inspected typeof args[0] === 'string' and args[0].url; native URL objects lack a .url property so it resolved to an empty string and _isExternalRequest('') returned false, letting external URL-object requests escape the sandbox. Naive substring checks (str.includes(...), str.startsWith('/')) were also spoofable via query-param injection, path injection, subdomain suffixing, and protocol-relative URLs, motivating the switch to canonical WHATWG URL hostname parsing with a strict allowlist and fail-closed catch block.

nodes.label: captureActiveFieldState / restoreActiveFieldState (Caret & Focus Preservation)
nodes.rationale: Live Firestore onSnapshot re-renders replace container.innerHTML wholesale, which would otherwise blur the active field, reset caret position, and discard uncommitted keystrokes; capturing id/value/selectionStart/selectionEnd before the re-render and restoring them afterward (with try/catch around setSelectionRange for input types like datetime-local that don't support it) lets a clinician keep typing uninterrupted while peer updates stream in.

nodes.label: ClinicalCryptoEngine (ML-KEM-768 + AES-256-GCM Hybrid PHI Encryption)
nodes.rationale: PHI must be protected against a future quantum-capable adversary, so encryption is designed as post-quantum FIPS 203 ML-KEM-768 hybrid key encapsulation combined with AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption; a random 12-byte IV per call gives semantic security, and any tampering fails the GCM auth tag and falls back to a safe placeholder string rather than leaking partially-decrypted PHI or throwing an unhandled error. A deterministic SIMULATED-ML-KEM-768 fallback keeps CI green where WebCrypto is unavailable.

nodes.label: diffPatientFields: Granular Multi-Clinician Field Diffing
nodes.rationale: Returning only the changed keys (instead of a full-document overwrite) lets Firestore's merge-based update apply just the local clinician's delta, so a concurrent peer edit to a different field (e.g. location) is never clobbered by a stale DOM snapshot of that field carried in the same form submission.

nodes.label: Offline Chaos Resilience & Dead-Letter-Queue Isolation
nodes.rationale: Under network flapping, a strict FIFO localStorage-backed queue with monotonic replay preserves clinical event ordering across reconnects, while a single malformed 'poison-pill' payload is routed to a dead_letter_queue instead of blocking the rest of the queue, so one corrupt transaction cannot stall synchronization of all other valid clinical updates.

nodes.label: NetworkIsolationGatekeeper Sandbox Escape Vulnerability
nodes.rationale: CHALLENGE_FAILED — _isExternalRequest relied on naive substring matching (str.includes/startsWith) instead of canonical URL parsing, so fetch(new URL(...)) (empty .url property), substring-spoofed hosts (https://evil.com/firestore.googleapis.com), and protocol-relative URLs (//evil.com/leak) all bypassed the sandbox lock without throwing SECURITY_EXCEPTION, violating the zero-PHI-exfiltration requirement.

nodes.norm_label: canonical whatwg url parsing remediation for networkisolationgatekeeper
nodes.rationale: Fix replaced substring/prefix matching with new URL(str, baseOrigin) hostname extraction, explicit args[0] href/url normalization for String/URL/Request inputs, protocol-relative detection (startsWith('/') && !startsWith('//')), and fail-closed try/catch classifying malformed URLs as external — resolving all four escape vectors challenger_2 identified.

nodes.rationale: Worker added an else-branch in initAuthListener plus explicit usersContainer.innerHTML='' and usersUnsubscribe?.()/patientsUnsubscribe?.()/unsubscribeRemoteConfig?.() invocations in showSignedOut() and showAccessGate(), guaranteeing DOM and subscription cleanup at every session exit point, in direct response to Bug 1 and Bug 2 raised by Challenger 2.

nodes.rationale: Generating an AI discharge summary automatically unchecks the attestation checkbox so a clinician cannot save or discharge without actively re-confirming they reviewed the AI-generated content, preventing rubber-stamped discharges.

nodes.label: diffPatientFields (Concurrency-Safe Field Diffing)
nodes.rationale: Only the minimal changed-field delta is written to Firestore so concurrent edits by peer clinicians on the same patient card are not silently overwritten.

nodes.label: EdgeAIClinicalEngine
nodes.rationale: On-device ESI scoring and discharge-summary synthesis run locally (Gemini Nano when available, a deterministic 5-part template otherwise) so patient PHI never has to leave the device for AI processing.

nodes.label: NetworkIsolationGatekeeper
nodes.rationale: Intercepts fetch/XHR/sendBeacon/WebSocket/EventSource during local AI inference to guarantee zero outbound network requests while PHI is being processed on-device, then unlocks and scrubs memory after.

nodes.label: Firestore Security Rules Generator (Enterprise)
nodes.rationale: Generated rules must be presented as an unproven, humble prototype rather than a security guarantee, so users are never misled about how protected their app actually is before a human review/hardening pass.

nodes.label: Firestore Indexes Reference
nodes.rationale: Sequentially increasing fields (e.g. timestamps) should be exempted from automatic single-field indexing because indexing them caps a collection's write throughput to roughly 500 writes/second.

nodes.label: Firestore Provisioning Guide
nodes.rationale: Firebase config files should be created manually rather than via `firebase init`, because that command expects interactive input that is incompatible with automated/agent-driven workflows.

nodes.label: Firestore Security Rules Generator (Standard)
nodes.rationale: Generated rules must be presented as an unproven, humble prototype rather than a security guarantee, so users are never misled about how protected their app actually is before a human review/hardening pass.

nodes.label: Firebase Security Rules Auditor Skill
nodes.rationale: Field-restriction checks like hasOnly()/diff() are insufficient alone because they only constrain which fields may change, not who may change them; without a paired ownership check, a collaborator could silently mutate another user's document fields — treated as a data-integrity vulnerability.

nodes.label: Firestore iOS Setup Guide
nodes.rationale: FirebaseFirestoreSwift must never be used post-SDK-v11 since its features merged into FirebaseFirestore; Firestore.firestore() must be lazily initialized to avoid a fatal crash if instantiated before FirebaseApp.configure(); and SwiftUI snapshot listeners must be tied to .task(id:) plus deinit rather than onDisappear, because presenting a sheet/cover triggers onDisappear on the underlying view (which would wrongly pause the listener) and because addSnapshotListener is synchronous so a bare .task would not auto-cancel it.

nodes.label: Firebase Remote Config Basics Skill
nodes.rationale: Fetched Remote Config values should be activated immediately at startup while new values fetch in the background for the next launch, minimizing user wait time; template edits made through the CLI must be verified by a human before deployment.

nodes.label: Xcode Project Setup Skill
nodes.rationale: Ruby/xcodeproj-gem scripting and manual .pbxproj edits are forbidden because modern Xcode folder synchronization already auto-includes files written to disk; a bundled Swift script is used instead for safe, idempotent SPM setup. The -ObjC linker flag must be injected for Firebase SPM products because static linking otherwise strips the Objective-C +load methods/categories Firebase depends on, causing fatal runtime crashes.
